课题组介绍

干旱区农业遥感课题组

面向干旱区农业，以服务粮食安全和耕地保护为主线，聚焦盐碱遥感与修复、资源调查与评估、时空融合、低空遥感与 GeoAI，把遥感方法真正用到田间地头。

研究方向

以服务粮食安全和耕地保护为主线，从机理建模一直做到业务化应用。以上任意方向胜任者皆可联系。

gxy3s@xju.edu.cn

葛翔宇

副教授、硕士生导师

葛翔宇，博士，副教授，硕导，遥感专业领域技术经理人（高级），担任国际数字地球学会中国国家委员会成像光谱对地观测专业委员会、中国自然资源学会研学工作委员会委员，主要从事农业遥感等研究。近 3 年主持国家自然科学基金青年基金（C 类）、新疆自然科学基金面上项目等项目 8 项。在 CATENA、JAG 等期刊发表高水平 SCI 论文，其中入选 ESI 全球高被引论文 7 篇，热点论文 1 篇；发明专利 3 项，软著 13 项，作为主要参与人立项地方标准 2 项、发布团体标准 2 项。入选天池英才、全球前 2% 科学家榜单、中国知网高被引学者，获第十六届自治区自然科学优秀学术论文二等奖。担任 Earth、Innovation Geoscience 等期刊编委、青年编委。

农业遥感盐碱地遥感高光谱遥感生态水文GeoAI
01
🟤

多尺度盐碱地遥感

盐碱地水盐垂直迁移快、空间异质性高、时间波动性大，单一尺度难以完整刻画。我们以多尺度遥感为核心范式：区域尺度构建长时序剖面数据产品及未来预测，流域尺度研发绿洲智能评估框架，田块尺度开展时空、空谱融合协同棉田水盐反演精细诊断，点位尺度利用物理模型进行水盐变化模拟与同化。

02
🌾

农业遥感与耕地保护

面向新疆耕地保护与农业管理需求，我们构建新疆作物光谱库，开展基于小样本的撂荒地识别、高光谱遥感与知识引导相结合的作物分类、耕地质量监测与评估以及农情监测，形成从光谱数据到耕地质量与农情信息的技术链条。

03
🛰️

无人机遥感

无人机遥感为田块尺度提供厘米级、高重访的观测数据。我们围绕其数据处理与信息提取开展研究：发展轻量级目标检测算法，实现田间小目标的快速识别；采用分数阶导数算法实现无人机高光谱影像降噪和特征提取；反演土壤水分、土壤盐分与冠层生理生化参数，支撑田块尺度的精细诊断。

04
💧

生态水文

中亚干旱区水资源稀缺，湿地与植被的格局和功能受水文过程强烈制约。我们以生态水文过程为主线：识别湿地水文要素，评估区域植被碳水利用效率，量化生态功能与生态服务价值，并诊断生态阈值，支撑干旱区生态保护与水资源管理。

学习资源

Python 基础与时空分析→

从零基础到时空分析：变量与容器、流程控制、函数、面向对象、常用标准库，再到数据统计、空间分析与时空分析。32 幕交互课程，单个 HTML 文件、完全离线可用。

Python零基础时空分析

R 语言基础与时空建模→

Research group

Arid-Region Agricultural Remote Sensing Group

We develop remote sensing methods for agriculture in arid regions, with a focus on food security and cropland protection. Our work covers remote sensing and reclamation of salt-affected soils, land resource surveys and assessment, spatiotemporal fusion, UAV remote sensing and GeoAI, and we apply these methods directly in the field.

Research

Our work runs from process-based modeling to operational applications, with food security and cropland protection as the common goal. If your background fits any of the topics below, please get in touch.

gxy3s@xju.edu.cn

Xiangyu Ge

Associate Professor and Master's Supervisor

Xiangyu Ge, PhD, is an Associate Professor and master's supervisor at Xinjiang University and a certified senior technology manager in remote sensing. He is a member of the Imaging Spectroscopy Earth Observation Committee of the Chinese National Committee of the International Society for Digital Earth, and of the Research-Based Learning Working Committee of the China Society of Natural Resources. His research focuses on agricultural remote sensing. In the past three years he has led eight projects as principal investigator, including an NSFC Young Scientists Fund project (Category C) and a General Program project of the Natural Science Foundation of Xinjiang. He has published in journals such as CATENA and JAG; seven of these papers are ESI Highly Cited Papers and one is an ESI Hot Paper. He holds three invention patents and 13 software copyrights. As a principal contributor, he has helped secure approval for two local standards and publish two association standards. He has been selected for the Tianchi Talent Program and named in the World's Top 2% Scientists list and the CNKI Highly Cited Scholars list, and he received a second prize in the 16th Xinjiang Outstanding Natural Science Academic Paper Awards. He serves on the editorial boards (including youth editorial boards) of journals such as Earth and The Innovation Geoscience.

Agricultural remote sensingSoil salinityHyperspectral remote sensingEcohydrologyGeoAI
01
🟤

Multi-scale remote sensing of soil salinity

In salt-affected soils, water and salts move rapidly through the profile and vary strongly in space and time, so no single observation scale can capture them fully. We therefore work across four scales. At the regional scale, we produce long-term, depth-resolved soil salinity products and future projections. At the watershed scale, we develop intelligent assessment frameworks for oases. At the field scale, we combine spatiotemporal and spatial–spectral fusion to retrieve soil moisture and salinity in cotton fields in fine detail. At the point scale, we use process-based models to simulate and assimilate water–salt dynamics.

02
🌾

Agricultural remote sensing and cropland protection

To support cropland protection and agricultural management in Xinjiang, we are building a regional crop spectral library. Building on it, we map abandoned cropland with limited training samples, classify crops by combining hyperspectral data with prior knowledge, monitor and assess cropland quality, and track crop condition. Together, these studies form a workflow that turns spectral measurements into usable information on cropland quality and crop status.

03
🛰️

UAV remote sensing

UAVs provide centimeter-resolution imagery at the field scale and can be flown as often as needed. Our UAV work focuses on data processing and information extraction. We develop lightweight object detection networks to detect small targets in the field quickly, and use fractional-order derivative (FOD) processing to denoise UAV hyperspectral imagery and extract spectral features. On this basis, we retrieve soil moisture, soil salinity and canopy physiological and biochemical traits for field-scale diagnosis.

04
💧

Ecohydrology

Water is scarce across arid Central Asia, and hydrological processes strongly control the distribution and functioning of wetlands and vegetation. Our work is organized around ecohydrological processes: we identify wetland hydrological components, assess the carbon and water use efficiency of regional vegetation, quantify ecosystem functions and ecosystem service values, and detect ecological thresholds. This work informs ecological conservation and water resource management in drylands.

Teaching

We teach remote sensing and GIS courses at the undergraduate, master's and doctoral levels. This page also brings together our teaching reform projects, textbook development and student competition results.

Learning resources

Python Fundamentals and Spatiotemporal Analysis→

A 32-lesson interactive course for complete beginners. It starts with variables and containers, control flow, functions, object-oriented programming and the standard library, then moves on to statistics, spatial analysis and spatiotemporal analysis. Delivered as a single HTML file that runs fully offline.

PythonBeginnerSpatiotemporal

R Fundamentals and Spatiotemporal Modeling→

A 26-chapter R course for geoscience and remote sensing. It covers vectors, data structures, data frames and dplyr/ggplot2; time-series decomposition and forecasting; sf and coordinate reference systems; raster processing with terra/stars; space–time cubes and kriging; and spatial regression and point pattern analysis. Delivered as a single HTML file that runs fully offline.

RSpatiotemporal modelingGeostatistics

SCI Writing in Remote Sensing and Geography→

An SCI writing module for graduate students in remote sensing and geography. It sets out the writing essentials from framing a topic and structuring the argument, through figures, to submission and revision. Hosted on GitHub and updated regularly.

SCI writingAcademic EnglishGraduate

UAV Remote Sensing: Interactive ModuleComing soon

An interactive teaching module based on the group's UAV hyperspectral platform. Under development.

Join Us

A mentor lays the base; their students set the pace. Today’s learners aim beyond degrees, and chart new paths with grace.

Master's students

Students are admitted through the college's regular admissions and recommended (exam-exempt) admission. We welcome applicants with backgrounds in remote sensing, GIS, surveying and mapping, computer science, agronomy, or resources and environmental science.

Annual intakeEarly contact welcome

Undergraduate research

As an innovation and entrepreneurship mentor at Xinjiang University, I supervise Student Research Training (SRT) projects and student competitions. My students have won several awards, including a national third prize in the iCAN competition.

SRT projectsCompetitions

How to apply

  1. Email me your CV and transcript, along with two or three sentences on the research topic you would like to pursue.
  2. Suggested subject line: “MSc application – Your name – Undergraduate university – Research interest”. I usually reply within a week.
  3. If there seems to be a good fit, I will arrange a 20–30 minute meeting, online or in person, to talk about what you have done and what you would like to do.

gxy3s@xju.edu.cn

A successful venture should start with a good plan and with clear goals set. We should boost confidence, build momentum to press ahead, and keep building small wins into major victories. The road is tortuous, but the future is bright. The darkness will soon pass, and the sun will break through. Frequently a favourable situation recurs and the initiative is regained as a result of “holding out a little longer”!
